EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows hallmark features of a monosubstituted benzene with an alkyl group: a very strong out-of-plane C–H bend near 721 cm⁻¹, aromatic C=C stretches at 1590 and 1567 cm⁻¹, and typical in-plane ring/CH bends around 1040–1200 cm⁻¹. The aliphatic C–H stretch bands at 2862 and 2913 cm⁻¹ (broad) and the deformation near 1449 cm⁻¹ are consistent with an ethyl side chain. There is no NH stretch (∼3300–3500 cm⁻¹) or SH stretch (∼2550–2620 cm⁻¹), disfavoring amine and thiol candidates; and no distinct SO₂ or strong C–F signatures. Ethylbenzene (candidate 10) best matches these Raman features.
